requirement:
An override preserves the requested scope and semantics, including the selected
language definition for parsing and structural search.
rationale:
The tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.sources.provider_results`. The requirement says that an override preserves the requested scope and semantics, including the selected language definition for parsing and structural search. Its two refining children, `provider_results.parse_snapshot` and `provider_results.search_completeness`, are separately marked and tested.

The obligations and the tests that cover them, all in `crates/habeas-sdk/tests/sources.rs`:

- **Requested scope reaches the primitives and overrides.**
  - `Memory` and `CachedParse` both list a `src/…` resource and an `other/…` resource whatever scope they are given. This means the scope has to be applied by the SDK defaults.
  - `defaults_use_provider_primitives_and_keep_one_parse_snapshot` searches text with the prefix `src`. It asserts exactly 2 matches and that the event log contains only `src/one.txt` reads plus one `list`, so `other/two.txt` is never read.
  - `structural_search_uses_overridden_parses_their_snapshot_and_requested_scope` runs structural search over `CachedParse`, which overrides `parse`, with the prefix `src`. It asserts a single match on `src/one.rs`, `fn[cached]`, with excerpt `call()`. A scope that was not applied would also match `other/two.rs`, because the fixture returns the same content for both. It also asserts exactly 3 parse calls for 3 queries, so one out-of-scope parse per query would be caught.
- **A parse override is used by structural search and keeps its own snapshot.** In `CachedParse`, `read` returns an error, so structural search can succeed only through the overridden `parse`. The test asserts the node's resource and excerpt. `list_read_only_provider_supports_selected_language_parse_and_structural_search` covers the mismatch case: it asserts that a parse override returning a different resource is an error ("parse returned a different resource").
- **The selected language definition applies to parsing and structural search.**
  - `list_read_only_provider_supports_selected_language_parse_and_structural_search` parses with the registry and asserts that `fn[provided]` resolves.
  - A structural query with language `rust` finds `call()` in `fn[provided]`.
  - A `python` query over the Rust source gives a complete, empty result.
  - An unknown language name is an error.
  - A resource's explicit language wins over its `.py` extension.
  - With no explicit language, the `.rs` extension selects Rust.
  - Malformed structural rules are an error.
- **Text search semantics through the defaults.** `defaults_use_provider_primitives_and_keep_one_parse_snapshot` checks `context_lines: 1` with the excerpt `"version 2\nhit one\nhit two"`. It also checks the match line number and that parsed results stay on the version-0 snapshot after a newer read.
- **Limit and completeness semantics.** `completeness_is_false_only_when_a_match_is_omitted_and_errors_propagate` and the structural test cover limits `None`, `Some(2)`, `Some(1)` and `Some(0)`, with matching `complete` values. They also check that a bad regex, invalid bytes and an unknown language are errors rather than complete empty results.

The tests have no separate case where a provider overrides `search_text` or `search_structure` itself. What the SDK can check is that its defaults, and its calls into overridden operations, preserve scope, language and snapshot semantics, and the tests check exactly that. How a provider's own override behaves is outside the SDK, and the requirement text states no further obligation to test. I found no unacknowledged gap.

text: :::{req} provider_results
An override preserves the requested scope and semantics, including the selected
language definition for parsing and structural search.
:::{req} language_provider
The language interface lives in `habeas-language`:
```rust,ignore
use tree_sitter::Language;
pub trait LanguageProvider: Sync {
/// Rules mapping syntax to named outline items.
fn profile(&'static self) -> &'static Profile;
/// The tree-sitter grammar used to parse the resource.
fn grammar(&self) -> fn() -> Language;
:::{req} local_provider
The SDK supplies a local-filesystem provider for listing and reading resources
within an application-selected scope.
:::{req} fence_precedence
Colon directive fences use three or more colons and support nested directives
with shorter inner fences. A colon-only closing fence has at least as many
colons as its opener.
Backtick and tilde code fences follow CommonMark rules and shield their contents
from colon-directive recognition. Fence-like text in inline code or raw HTML
introduces no outline directive blocks.
:::{req} fenced_blocks
Colon-fenced directives and fenced code blocks have anonymous `block` nodes
with selectors under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
A block contains its opening fence, body, and closing fence when present.
Its parent is the nearest enclosing outline container.
:::{req} fenced_blocks.contents
Colon-fenced directive bodies are outlined recursively as Markdown. Ordinary
fenced code-block contents remain literal, creating no nested paragraph or
directive nodes.
:::{req} paragraphs
Each prose paragraph has an anonymous `paragraph` node under its nearest
enclosing outline container. This includes paragraphs before the first heading
and inside list items, quotations, and directive bodies. Their selectors follow
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Heading text and literal
code-block contents create no paragraph nodes.
:::{req} provider
The SDK exposes a source-provider interface for enumerating resource identities
within a requested scope and reading resource bytes. Resources need no local
filesystem path.
:::{req} provider.errors
Listing and reading failures are errors, distinct from successful empty
listings and successful reads of empty resources.
:::{req} provider_defaults
Source providers can override parsing, text search, and structural search.
The SDK supplies defaults for all three, so listing, reading, and a supplied
language registry suffice to support them.
:::{req} provider_defaults.composition
The defaults compose through the provider's operations:
| Default operation | Uses |
| Parsing | Provider reading and the selected language definition |
| Text search | Provider listing and reading |
| Structural search | Provider listing and parsing, including any parsing override |
:::{req} provider_observations
The tracked inspection context records successful source-node reads delivered
to the procedure as assessment dependencies, whether the provider uses defaults
or overrides. Each fingerprint describes the contents delivered to the caller.
:::{req} provider_results
An override preserves the requested scope and semantics, including the selected
language definition for parsing and structural search.
:::{req} provider_results.parse_snapshot
A parse result retains the source snapshot it describes. A cached parse stays
paired with those bytes, rather than bytes from a different source snapshot.
:::{req} provider_results.search_completeness
Search results distinguish complete results from truncated or incomplete
ones. An operation failure is an error, rather than a complete empty result.
